title: Treatment resistance in personality disorders
bottleneck: Personality disorders (especially borderline and antisocial) involve deeply ingrained patterns of thinking and behavior with high suicide and comorbidity rates, yet no drug treats the disorder itself and evidence-based psychotherapies (DBT, MBT) require a year or more of intensive treatment that few systems provide. Research funding is minimal relative to burden.
why_it_blocks: These are among the most stigmatized and undertreated conditions in psychiatry, with patients cycling through crisis services for decades. The absence of scalable treatments guarantees chronicity.
current_state: Dialectical behavior therapy has the strongest evidence for borderline personality disorder; delivery is limited by therapist training and cost. Pharmacotherapy remains symptom-targeted and off-label. Mentalization-based and schema therapies show durable benefits in trials, but training enough therapists to meet demand would take a generation at current rates.
